definitions.definition: ell=Int.toNat(λ). When λ≥0 its integer image is λ; this equality is used only under the stated nonnegativity hypothesis.
I={0,...,ell}, equivalently Fin(n), of cardinal n. Index arithmetic in factorials and binomials is natural arithmetic; for each i∈I the scalar weight ell−2i uses integer subtraction before casting.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ, X_r=(r! as a complex scalar)^{-1} x^r. Products of endomorphisms mean composition, rightmost factor first.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ, Y_r=(r! as a complex scalar)^{-1} y^r.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the complex universal enveloping algebra of sl₂
definitions.definition: U_Z is the ℤ-subalgebra generated by x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r, acting on V through the given representation; these actions are X_r and Y_r.
U=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K. K acts on the K factor. For any ℤ-endomorphism fU of M its induced operator on U sends mU⊗αU to fU(mU)⊗αU, for all mU∈M and αU∈K.

definitions.type: K-Lie algebra with its induced action on U
definitions.definition: L_K=L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K in the original Chevalley construction. Its action on U is induced from the lattice restrictions of x,y,h and extended K-linearly; the integral Chevalley lattice is used also in characteristic 2.
For i∈I define e_i=Y_i v=y^i v/i!. This definition does not assert that e is a basis.
For j∈I, c_j=binom(ell,j). A bar over any integer or natural coefficient below means its image under ℤ→K.
C=∏_{j∈I} c_j; the empty product is 1.
For i∈I, d_i=∏_{j∈I,j≠i} c_j, with empty product 1.
Q=Y_ell X_ell. This is the operator called P in basis-proof.md; Q avoids conflict with the target ID P.

For i,j∈I, a_ij is the restriction of A_ij to M. Admissibility ensures that each divided-power factor preserves M and thus that this restriction exists. Superscript M on an operator denotes its restriction to M whenever preservation has been established. The existence and commutator formula for h^M are proved explicitly.
T=K⊗_ℤ M, with scalar action on the K factor.

definitions.type: scalar-extension operation on ℤ-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For f∈End_ℤ(M), hat(f)=LinearMap.baseChange K f∈End_K(T), the canonical scalar extension. Write x̂=hat(x^M), ŷ=hat(y^M), ĥ=hat(h^M), X̂_r=hat(X_r^M), Ŷ_r=hat(Y_r^M) when the lattice restrictions exist. The pure-tensor evaluation formula is established through the registered scalar-extension theorem.
F_ij=(c_j as a scalar in K)^{-1} hat(a_ij). Inversion uses the field's total inverse; nonzeroness of c_j is proved subsequently, not assumed in this definition.

inputs.statement: M⊂V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z (equivalently under every X_r,Y_r for r≥0). M is not assumed minimal.

For each j∈I, c_j>0 and c_j j!(ell−j)!=ell!, and binom(ell,ell−j)=c_j. On the complex basis e, Q e_ell=e_ell and Q e_k=0 for k<ell. For every i,j,k∈I, A_ij e_k=c_j e_i if k=j and is zero otherwise. Every A_ij preserves M and its restriction is a_ij. The following are equalities of ℤ-endomorphisms of M: for all i,j,k,l∈I, a_ij a_kl=c_j a_il if j=k, and zero otherwise; ∑_{i∈I} d_i a_ii=C Id_M; and C=c_i d_i for each i∈I. For every natural r, r! X_r^M=(x^M)^r and r! Y_r^M=(y^M)^r. The restrictions of x,y,h exist and h^M=x^M y^M−y^M x^M.

ell has integer image λ and ell<p; n=ell+1>0. T is a nonzero finite-dimensional K-vector space with dimension n. For every natural r≤ell, (r! as a scalar in K)≠0. Each c_j (j∈I) and C has nonzero image in K. The endomorphisms F of T satisfy, for all i,j,k,l∈I, F_ij F_kl=F_il when j=k and are zero otherwise, and ∑_{i∈I} F_ii=Id_T. Scalar extension hat preserves addition, integer scalar multiplication, composition, identity, finite sums and powers. For r≤ell, X̂_r=(r! as a scalar in K)^{-1}x̂^r and Ŷ_r=(r! as a scalar in K)^{-1}ŷ^r; ĥ=x̂ŷ−ŷx̂. For every f0∈End_ℤ(M), α0∈K and m0∈M, hat(f0)(α0⊗m0)=α0⊗f0(m0).
The complex-linear Chevalley operators satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h; v≠0, xv=0, hv=λv.

output.statement: U=M⊗_ℤ K is a nonzero finite-dimensional K-vector space of dimension n=ell+1>0. There exists a family G:I×I→End_K(U) with all of the following properties: for all i,j,k,l∈I, G_ij G_kl=G_il if j=k and zero otherwise; ∑_{i∈I}G_ii=Id_U; and every K-linear subspace W⊂U invariant under the original induced x,y actions is invariant under all G_ij. The induced h action is the commutator of the induced x and y actions. The representation is precisely the original L_K action, also in characteristic 2.

argument.text: Construct s:U→T by m⊗α↦α⊗m and t:T→U by α⊗m↦m⊗α. Each assignment is additive in each argument. For z∈ℤ, (zm)⊗α=m⊗(zα) is sent to α⊗(zm)=(zα)⊗m, exactly the balance relation in T; the reverse check is identical. The tensor universal property therefore gives additive maps, which are K-linear for the scalar action on the K factor. Both composites fix every pure tensor, hence are identities since pure tensors generate the tensor spaces. For any ℤ-endomorphism f of M, s(f(m)⊗α)=α⊗f(m)=hat(f)(s(m⊗α)) by N003. Thus s,t are inverse K-linear maps intertwining every induced lattice operator.

produces.statement: s:U→T and t:T→U are inverse K-linear maps. For every f0∈End_ℤ(M), s intertwines the induced f0 action on U with hat(f0) on T.

argument.text: Fix any K-subspace W of T and assume L1: W is invariant under x̂ and ŷ. The identity preserves W. Inductively, if the r-th power of either operator preserves W, applying that operator once more shows its (r+1)-st power preserves W. Thus all their natural powers preserve W. By N003 and closure under K-scalar multiplication, W is invariant under X̂_r,Ŷ_r for every r≤ell. N002 expresses a_ij as the composition of the four restrictions X_{ell−i},Y_ell,X_ell,Y_{ell−j}. Scalar extension preserves this composition by N003. All four indices lie between 0 and ell, so W is invariant under hat(a_ij), then under its scalar multiple F_ij. Discharge L1 and quantify over W: every x̂,ŷ-invariant subspace of T is invariant under every F_ij.

produces.statement: For every K-subspace Wt of T, if Wt is invariant under x̂ and ŷ, it is invariant under all F_{ii,jj}, ii,jj∈I.

argument.text: Define G_ij=t F_ij s. Because st=Id_T and ts=Id_U from F001, multiplication and the sum relation in N003 transport to G_ij G_kl=G_il for j=k and zero otherwise, and ∑_i G_ii=Id_U. The same K-linear equivalence transports nonzeroness, finite-dimensionality and dim T=n from N003 to U. For any K-subspace of U invariant under its original induced x,y operators, its image under s is invariant under x̂,ŷ by F001; F002 makes that image invariant under every F_ij. Applying t proves the original subspace invariant under every G_ij. The commutator identity for ĥ in N003 and the intertwinings show that the transported h is exactly the original induced h. H005, H006 and N002 ensure all lattice restrictions exist, so D008 gives precisely the prescribed L_K action. We have thus constructed the claimed family for the original U=M⊗_ℤ K.
